records.content_text:
The table in the previous section listed the names of large numbers made up of groups of ten. This table shows how to write numbers as powers of ten.

$$
\begin{array}{|l|l|l|}
  \hline
    \textbf{Name} & \textbf{Number} & \textbf{Powers of ten}  \\
    \hline
     \text{Ten} & 10 & 10=10^1    \\
    \hline
     \text{Hundred} & 100 & 10\times10=10^2    \\
    \hline
    \text{Thousand} & 1,000 & 10\times10\times10=10^3    \\
    \hline
    \text{Ten thousand} & 10,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10=10^4    \\
    \hline
    \text{Hundred thousand} & 100,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^5    \\
    \hline
    \text{Million} & 1,000,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^6    \\
    \hline
    \text{Ten million} & 10,000,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^7 \\
    \hline
    \text{Hundred million} & 100,000,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^8 \\
    \hline
    \text{Billion} & 1,000,000,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^9 \\
    \hline
     \end{array}
$$

The number 1,000,000,000 is named one billion. Try to imagine how large one billion is:

- One billion seconds from your birth, you will be just over 31 years and 8 months old.
- One billion sheets of photocopy paper stacked on top of each other would reach almost 110 km into the sky.

We may count from zero to ten million in millions:
0: zero

Worked example 1.4: Counting with large numbers

Count in thousands from five hundred and sixty one million seven hundred and twenty one thousand to five hundred and sixty one million seven hundred and thirty two thousand. Write down the numbers and their names.

  1. Step 1: Write both numbers in a place value table.

  2. Step 2: Look closely at the first place value table. Decide in which column the digit must increase as you are counting.

    If you count in thousands, the digit in the "th" column must increase.

  3. Step 3: Increase the digit in the column you identified by 1 and write down the number. Continue until you reach the digit 9.

    561,724,000
    561,725,000
    561,726,000
    561,727,000
    561,728,000
    561,729,000

  4. Step 4: Deal with the digit 9 as you did before. Change it to 0 and add 1 to the column to its left. Add the number to your list.

    561,724,000

    561,727,000

    561,730,000

records.prompt_text: Express 0.15 billion in digits only. Write out the full name of the answer.
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Write down the meaning of the mixed number.

0.15 billion means 0.15 of a group of 1,000,000,000:
$0.15\times1,000,000,000$

Step 2: Do the calculation.

- "Ignore" the decimal point at first.
  $15\times1,000,000,000=15,000,000,000$
- Insert a decimal point in your answer. You must have the same number of digits after the decimal point as there are altogether in the original numbers: 1,000,000,000 does not have a decimal point and 0.15 has two digits after the decimal point, so you need two digits after the decimal point in your answer.
  $15,000,000,000$ becomes $15,000,000,0.00$
- If there are zeros at the end of the number after the decimal point, you can leave them out. Rewrite the number and regroup it correctly.
  $150000000=150,000,000$

- The numbers from 0 to 999 have no grouping commas.
- The numbers from 1,000 to 999,999 have only one grouping comma.
- The numbers from 1,000,000 to 999,999,999 have two grouping commas.
- The numbers from 1,000,000,000 to 999,999,999,999 have three grouping commas.

150,000,000 has two grouping commas, so it is in the millions. Its full name is: one hundred and fifty million.
